item.title: Constitutional Review Commission to submit final report to President today
item.description: The Constitutional Review Commission will submit its final report on the review of the 2013 Constitution to President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu today, marking a major milestone in the six-month review process. The submission follows the completion of the Commission's six-month review.
item.content:encoded:
The Constitutional Review Commission will submit its final report on the review of the 2013 Constitution to President Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu today, marking a major milestone in the six-month review process.

The submission follows the completion of the Commission's six-month review.

The Commission says the final report reflects the views, concerns and aspirations shared by Fijians during the public consultation process.

item.title: Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm Friday September 4th
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Barisal, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

You can also be part of the live audience by applying for registration with a question that you would like to ask during the forum.

The application to register details can be found on our website and facebook page, fijivillage.

You will receive a confirmation if you have been selected to be part of the live audience.

Please apply early to avoid any disappointment.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm Friday September 4th on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: Nadarivatu Blue-light camp helps young people build skills for life
item.description: Young people who took part in the Nadarivatu Blue-light camp are being encouraged to take the skills and values they learnt back to their homes, schools and communities after completing the week-long programme. Deputy Divisional Police Commander West, Superintendent of Police Esira Bari says the camp was not only about activities and having fun, but also about helping participants develop into res
item.content:encoded:
Young people who took part in the Nadarivatu Blue-light camp are being encouraged to take the skills and values they learnt back to their homes, schools and communities after completing the week-long programme.

Deputy Divisional Police Commander West, Superintendent of Police Esira Bari says the camp was not only about activities and having fun, but also about helping participants develop into responsible and confident young people.

Bari says participants were taught important values including respect, discipline, responsibility, teamwork, resilience, confidence and leadership.

He says the real value of the camp will be seen in how participants apply these lessons in their everyday lives.

Bari encouraged the young people to practise what they learnt and reminded them that the decisions they make will help shape their future.

He also urged parents to continue supporting their children after the camp by listening to them, asking about their experiences and encouraging them to put the lessons they learnt into practice.

Bari says parents should recognise that their children are returning home with new experiences, skills and lessons that can help them grow.

The camp was organised through Fiji Police Community Policing in partnership with Blue Light Fiji, Blue Light New Zealand and other partners.

item.title: At least 794 dead, more than 2,500 missing after Nepal flash floods
item.description: At least 794 people have died and more than 2,500 remain missing following devastating flash floods in Nepal. Nepal Police says 794 bodies had been recovered as of yesterday.
item.content:encoded:
At least 794 people have died and more than 2,500 remain missing following devastating flash floods in Nepal.

Nepal Police says 794 bodies had been recovered as of yesterday.

However, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority says 781 people have been killed and 2,502 remain missing.

The figures from different agencies continue to vary as rescue and recovery efforts continue.

The flash floods struck on Wednesday, causing widespread destruction and affecting communities, tourist areas and hydropower sites.

Hundreds of those missing are believed to be workers at Nepal's hydropower sites.

Authorities are intensifying efforts to reach hundreds of people trapped inside a tunnel at the Trishuli-3A hydropower site.

Hundreds of foreign nationals are also reported missing.

At least 320 Indian nationals, nearly 100 Chinese nationals, 90 Americans, 62 Ukrainians, 51 Malaysians and 41 Australians are among those reported missing.

Nepal Police also says 33 British nationals are missing, while 30 Canadians have been reported missing.

Smaller numbers of travellers from South Korea, South Africa, Portugal, the Netherlands and New Zealand are also among those unaccounted for.

Meanwhile, Chinese state media says 16 people have died and 546 are missing in Tibet, where rescuers are continuing to search for survivors.

item.title: Vinal Kumar returns to Fiji after eight years to reconnect with family and his roots
item.description: 23-year-old Vinal Kumar has returned home after eight years away from Fiji to reconnect with family and friends, revisit places that shaped his childhood and enjoy the Fijian food he has missed. Originally from Vatuwaqa, Suva, with maternal links to Labasa, Kumar moved to the United States with his parents and now resides in Seattle, Washington, where he completed his education and works as a civi
item.content:encoded:
23-year-old Vinal Kumar has returned home after eight years away from Fiji to reconnect with family and friends, revisit places that shaped his childhood and enjoy the Fijian food he has missed.

Originally from Vatuwaqa, Suva, with maternal links to Labasa, Kumar moved to the United States with his parents and now resides in Seattle, Washington, where he completed his education and works as a civil engineer.

While speaking to fijivillage News, Kumar says returning to Fiji has brought back many memories.

He shares the return has also allowed him to reconnect with his mother's family in Labasa, where he visited the Naag Mandir and saw how much the area had developed since his last visit.

Insert: Kumar on trying Fijian Food 27th AUg

Meanwhile, he says he attended around 11 to 12 different primary schools in Fiji while growing up because both his parents were teachers and were transferred between schools.

These included Annesley Methodist, Nehru Memorial School, Samabula Sanatan, Swami Shraddhanand Memorial School, Vuanisaki Primary, Nasavusavu District, Naweni District and Samabula Primary.

Kumar later attended MGM High School for Year 10 before moving to the US, where he attended Auburn Riverside High School and Kent Meridian High School.

Hindi Insert:Kumar on school memories 27th Aug

He then attended Green River College,where he earned an Associate in Science (Engineering), before completing a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering at the University of Washington Tacoma.

Kumar says some of his fondest school memories include taking part in science and drama competitions.

He recalls participating in a drama that highlighted the importance of the Hindi language and encouraged students to value their mother tongue.

Kumar says moving to the USA also influenced his decision to pursue civil engineering.

He says seeing multi-lane highways, bridges and other major infrastructure made him curious about who designed and built them.

That interest eventually led him into civil engineering, and he now works as a consultant for a private company, designing roads for cities and towns.

Kumar says his parents, who are both teachers and are now teaching in the US, have supported him throughout his journey.

item.title: Hibiscus Dog Show and Pet Walk promotes kindness and better care for animals
item.description: Pet owners and animal lovers gathered at Albert Park for the Hibiscus Dog Show and Pet Walk, with the event being used to promote better care for animals and encourage people to treat them with kindness. Fiji SPCA Shelter Manager Shaneel Narayan says the event was organised in partnership with the Hibiscus Festival committee and was a success.
item.content:encoded:
Pet owners and animal lovers gathered at Albert Park for the Hibiscus Dog Show and Pet Walk, with the event being used to promote better care for animals and encourage people to treat them with kindness.

Fiji SPCA Shelter Manager Shaneel Narayan says the event was organised in partnership with the Hibiscus Festival committee and was a success.

Narayan says dogs competed in eight different categories, while a week-long cat competition was also held through the organisation's social media platforms.

He says Fiji SPCA will continue its animal welfare activities throughout the Hibiscus Festival, with a booth operating during the week.

Narayan says the SPCA will use its presence at the festival to provide education and raise awareness about animal welfare, as well as carry out vaccination and other animal care programmes.

He is encouraging people attending the Hibiscus Festival to visit the booth and learn more about responsible animal care and how they can better look after their pets.

Narayan says the message Fiji SPCA wants people to take away is simple — be kind to animals.
